title: Solving math word problems with process- and outcome-based feedback
notes: process_supervision: must-cite - the first head-to-head comparison of process- and outcome-based supervision (GSM8K), showing that final-answer correctness hides reasoning errors (trace error among answer-correct solutions cut from 14.0% to 3.4% only with process supervision), the gap EngTrace measures.

title: Math-Shepherd: Verify and Reinforce LLMs Step-by-step without Human Annotations
notes: process_supervision: must-cite - the canonical PRM trained on Monte Carlo rollout step labels instead of human labels, the automatic-labelling paradigm behind the off-the-shelf PRMs EngTrace tests; named in the plan of record.

title: ProcessBench: Identifying Process Errors in Mathematical Reasoning
notes: process_supervision: must-cite - the standard human-annotated first-error benchmark (3,400 math solutions) for PRMs and critic LLMs; EngTrace differs by being engineering, gold-trace-based and deterministic, and is named against it in the plan of record.

title: PRMBench: A Fine-grained and Challenging Benchmark for Process-Level Reward Models
notes: process_supervision: must-cite - fine-grained PRM benchmark (6,216 problems, 83,456 step labels, error categories under simplicity, soundness and sensitivity) showing PRMs well below human performance; math only, with constructed errors.

title: The Lessons of Developing Process Reward Models in Mathematical Reasoning
notes: process_supervision: must-cite - releases the Qwen2.5-Math-PRM 7B and 72B that EngTrace evaluates, and reports that Monte Carlo step labels are noisy and that Best-of-N evaluation rewards correct answers reached through flawed steps.

title: VersaPRM: Multi-Domain Process Reward Model via Synthetic Reasoning Data
notes: process_supervision: must-cite - the multi-domain PRM EngTrace evaluates; reports that math-trained PRMs transfer poorly outside math, the premise EngTrace tests on expert-labelled engineering traces.

title: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning Beyond Accuracy
notes: process_supervision: must-cite - ReasonEval scores each step for validity and redundancy and finds that higher final-answer accuracy does not imply better reasoning steps; the closest model-based analogue to EngTrace's process scores.

title: ROSCOE: A Suite of Metrics for Scoring Step-by-Step Reasoning
notes: process_supervision: must-cite - the canonical reference-free metric suite for step-by-step reasoning, the reasoning-specific counterpart to the BERTScore and ROUGE-2 metrics the May paper uses to score solutions against the gold trace (Sec. 4.3).

title: PRIME: A Process-Outcome Alignment Benchmark for Verifiable Reasoning in Mathematics and Engineering
notes: process_supervision: must-cite - benchmarks verifiers on process-outcome alignment (2,530 college-level STEM items, mathematics and engineering) to catch spurious correctness; the closest competitor to EngTrace's correct-answer, flawed-process finding, and an engineering one.

title: LSR-Ben: A Logical and Scientific Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Process Reward Models
notes: process_supervision: should-cite - PRM benchmark outside math (3,595 human-annotated first-error items, science and logic, nine subdomains; first titled GR-Ben) where Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-72B falls from 78.3 F1 on ProcessBench to 37.4 and PRMs tend to overlook errors; external corroboration of EngTrace's PRM result.

title: Hard2Verify: A Step-Level Verification Benchmark for Open-Ended Frontier Math
notes: process_supervision: should-cite - human-annotated step-level labels on frontier-model solutions to recent competition problems, where the same Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-72B that leads ProcessBench drops sharply; PRM scores do not transfer to harder, naturally occurring errors.

title: MR-GSM8K: A Meta-Reasoning Benchmark for Large Language Model Evaluation
notes: process_supervision: should-cite - meta-reasoning benchmark with human first-error-step and error-reason labels on GSM8K solutions; models close on GSM8K separate by over 20 points when asked to verify.

title: MR-Ben: A Meta-Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating System-2 Thinking in LLMs
notes: process_supervision: should-cite - expert-curated benchmark (5,975 questions incl. physics, chemistry, logic, coding) asking models to locate, explain and correct the first error in a solution; the nearest multi-domain step-error benchmark.

title: LLMs cannot find reasoning errors, but can correct them given the error location
notes: process_supervision: should-cite - BIG-Bench Mistake, CoT traces with human-annotated first logical mistake; LLMs fail to find even objective mistakes, which motivates non-LLM checks such as EngTrace's deterministic ones.

title: A Chain-of-Thought Is as Strong as Its Weakest Link: A Benchmark for Verifiers of Reasoning Chains
notes: process_supervision: should-cite - REVEAL, step-level human labels (relevance, attribution, logical correctness) for verifiers of open-domain QA chains; verifiers struggle most with logical correctness.

title: Can Large Language Models Detect Errors in Long Chain-of-Thought Reasoning?
notes: process_supervision: should-cite - DeltaBench, human-annotated error detection on long reasoning-model CoTs across math, code, physics/chemistry/biology and general reasoning; PRMs and critic LLMs both perform poorly.

title: ReCEval: Evaluating Reasoning Chains via Correctness and Informativeness
notes: process_supervision: should-cite - reference-free step evaluation by correctness (NLI) and informativeness (V-information); with ROSCOE, the pre-PRM baseline for evaluating reasoning chains.

title: Evaluating Step-by-step Reasoning Traces: A Survey
notes: process_supervision: should-cite - survey and taxonomy of trace-evaluation criteria and evaluators; one citation that places EngTrace's milestone and arithmetic checks in the field.

title: Generative Verifiers: Reward Modeling as Next-Token Prediction
notes: process_supervision: should-cite - generative verifiers (verification as next-token prediction, with chain-of-thought), the paradigm behind using an LLM as a step verifier, as EngTrace's residual judge does.

title: Process Reward Models That Think
notes: process_supervision: should-cite - ThinkPRM, a generative PRM writing a verification chain-of-thought, trained on about 1% of PRM800K's labels and beating discriminative PRMs and LLM-as-judge; the strongest recent alternative to the PRMs EngTrace tests.

title: GenPRM: Scaling Test-Time Compute of Process Reward Models via Generative Reasoning
notes: process_supervision: should-cite - generative PRM that executes code to verify each step's computation (7B beats Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-72B on ProcessBench); the program-aided step check closest to EngTrace's per-claim arithmetic rule.

title: Rethinking Reward Models for Multi-Domain Test-Time Scaling
notes: process_supervision: should-cite - unified 14-domain comparison of discriminative and generative outcome and process reward models: generative outcome verification is most robust, process scoring suffers label noise on long traces; the outcome-vs-process evidence beyond math.

title: PhysPRM: A Generative Process Reward Model with Fine-grained Diagnosis for Physics Problem Solving
notes: process_supervision: should-cite - physics PRM giving step critiques and error types, with a human-verified step-level benchmark (PhysProcessBench); the nearest science-domain process verifier to EngTrace's engineering setting.

title: From Answers to States: Verifiable Process-Level Evaluation of Chemical Reasoning in Large Language Models
notes: process_supervision: should-cite - ChemCoTBench-V2 checks intermediate chemical states with deterministic rule verifiers and reference traces and finds correct final answers over flawed steps; the closest methodological analogue to EngTrace's deterministic milestone checks.

title: Neuro-symbolic PRM: Enhancing Scientific Reasoning via Structured Traces and Symbolic Verification
notes: process_supervision: should-cite - splits step checking into symbolic validity (deterministic verifier: executable, unit-consistent) and semantic groundedness (a PRM), with hard negatives that pass the verifier yet are wrong; mirrors EngTrace's finding that deterministic checks miss conceptual defects.

title: The Answer Is Not the Argument
notes: process_supervision: should-cite - frontier-model physics traces (Humanity's Last Exam) labelled for answer correctness and first false step: some correct-answer traces hide genuine errors and giving monitors the answer lowers recall on them; independent evidence for EngTrace's correct-answer blind spot.

title: LLMs cannot spot math errors, even when allowed to peek into the solution
authors: KV Aditya Srivatsa, Kaushal Kumar Maurya, Ekaterina Kochmar
notes: process_supervision: should-cite - LLMs fail to locate the first error step in student solutions even with the reference solution in context; directly relevant to EngTrace's reference-guided residual judge.

title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
notes: process_supervision: optional - chain-of-thought can misstate why a model answered; supports a Limitations sentence that EngTrace scores the written trace, not the model's internal computation.

title: Beyond Outcome Verification: Verifiable Process Reward Models for Structured Reasoning
authors: Massimiliano Pronesti, Anya Belz, Yufang Hou
notes: process_supervision: optional - verifiable process rewards, where deterministic guideline-grounded verifiers check each step against gold (medical risk-of-bias assessment); a training-side counterpart to EngTrace's deterministic step checks.

title: SPARE: Single-Pass Annotation with Reference-Guided Evaluation for Automatic Process Supervision and Reward Modelling
authors: Md Imbesat Hassan Rizvi, Xiaodan Zhu, Iryna Gurevych
notes: process_supervision: optional - reference-guided step annotation that aligns each solution step to reference-solution steps; the LLM-based counterpart to EngTrace's gold-milestone coverage.
